hints: Notice the diagram shows two equal and opposite $F$ forces on opposite edges of the $4.0\text{ cm}$ radius lid, so they form a couple.
Recall the torque of a couple is one force multiplied by the perpendicular separation between them, which here is the diameter, not the radius.
Convert the $8.0\text{ cm}$ separation to $0.080\text{ m}$ and set $F \times 0.080\text{ m} = 20\text{ N m}$ to find $F$.
walkthrough: The lid radius is $4.0\text{ cm} = 0.040\text{ m}$, so the perpendicular distance between the two opposite $F$ forces is the diameter $d = 2 \times 0.040\text{ m} = 0.080\text{ m}$.
The two forces form a couple, so total torque $= F \times d$. Both forces turn the lid the same way, so their moments add.
Set the required torque equal to the couple torque: $F \times 0.080\text{ m} = 20\text{ N m}$.
Rearrange and substitute: $F = 20 / 0.080 = 250\text{ N}$, with units of $\text{N}$ as expected for force.

options.A: Gives $2.5\text{ N}$ by dividing by the diameter in cm, $20/8$, without converting $8.0\text{ cm}$ to $0.080\text{ m}$.
options.B: Gives $5.0\text{ N}$ by using $20/4.0$ without converting $4.0\text{ cm}$ to metres and without using the full separation of the couple.
options.C: The couple torque $F \times 0.080\text{ m} = 20\text{ N m}$ gives $F = 250\text{ N}$.
options.D: Gives $500\text{ N}$ from $F \times 0.040\text{ m} = 20\text{ N m}$, which counts only one force instead of the couple formed by both forces.
